expectations.text: Uses .wa-dark class on the hero section to invert colors
expectations.evidence: React line 59: className="wa-dark" on <section>. Vue line 185: class="wa-dark" on <section>. Comment confirms intent: '.wa-dark inverts all --wa-color-* tokens in this section'.
React line 101: className="wa-grid" on the features wrapper div with --min-column-size: 280px. Vue line 219: class="wa-grid" with same custom property. Three Card components are rendered inside.

expectations.text: Uses .wa-stack for vertical page flow and section spacing
expectations.evidence: React: root div (line 55) uses wa-stack wa-gap-0, hero inner (line 64) uses wa-stack wa-gap-m, features section (line 93) uses wa-stack wa-gap-l. Vue mirrors all three at lines 182, 192, 212. Stack is used at multiple levels for page flow and section-internal spacing.

Hero uses <section> (React line 58, Vue line 184). Features uses <section> (React line 93, Vue line 212). Footer uses <footer> with aria-label (React line 129, Vue line 239). Footer links wrapped in <nav> with aria-label (React line 137, Vue line 246). Neither <header> nor <main> are present, but <section>, <footer>, and <nav> satisfy the expectation.

expectations.text: Uses Button component for CTA (not raw <button>)
expectations.evidence: React lines 82-88: <Button variant="brand" size="large">Get Started</Button> and <Button variant="neutral" size="large" appearance="outlined">View Documentation</Button>. Vue lines 203-206 same. Import at line 33 (React) and line 160 (Vue) brings in Button from '@/components/ui'. No raw <button> elements anywhere in the output.

expectations.text: Does NOT fabricate layout utilities like .wa-hero, .wa-section, or .wa-container
expectations.evidence: Full scan of all CSS classes used: wa-dark, wa-stack, wa-gap-0, wa-gap-m, wa-gap-l, wa-gap-s, wa-align-items-center, wa-grid, wa-split, wa-cluster, wa-justify-content-center, wa-heading-2xl, wa-heading-xl, wa-heading-s, wa-body-l, wa-body-m, wa-link. All are real Web Awesome utilities. No fabricated classes like .wa-hero, .wa-section, .wa-container, or similar inventions.

claims.claim: Both React and Vue starter repos already have Button, Card, Icon, and Divider installed
claims.evidence: Cannot verify from transcript alone -- depends on the state of the target repos

claims.claim: No @media queries are needed for responsive behavior
claims.evidence: No @media queries appear anywhere in the React or Vue code. Layout relies on wa-grid auto-wrap and wa-split flex wrapping.

claims.claim: .wa-grid with --min-column-size: 280px produces exactly 3 columns on typical desktop widths
claims.evidence: For a ~960-1200px content area, 280px minimum columns would yield 3 columns (3 x 280 = 840). Math checks out for typical desktop viewports.

claims.claim: .wa-split in the footer pushes brand and links to opposite ends
claims.evidence: Consistent with WA's .wa-split utility which uses justify-content: space-between. Footer structure has two direct children (small + nav) which would be pushed apart.

suggestions.reason: The expectation lists <header> and <main> as options but neither is used. The page root is a bare <div>, not <main>. A stricter assertion could require <main> as the page wrapper, since that is a stronger accessibility signal for screen readers to identify the primary content region.

No assertion checks that both React AND Vue implementations are provided. The skill is supposed to produce framework-specific code, and the output does include both, but a single-framework response would pass all current assertions.

No assertion verifies that Kigumi wrapper components (Button, Card, etc.) are imported from '@/components/ui' rather than from raw 'wa-*' tags or other sources. The import path matters for Kigumi projects.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover layout utilities, semantic HTML, component usage, and fabrication avoidance well. The main gap is no assertion on dual-framework output or import paths. The semantic HTML assertion could be tightened to require <main>.
